title: Literary Arts and Narrative Design
answer: Agentic drafting, outlining, character dialogue, continuity tracking and developmental editing.

children.name: Agentic Drafting and Multi-Model Workflows
children.blurb: Agentic drafting and multi-model workflows describe a way of writing in which a language model is given a goal and a degree of autonomy, then allowed to plan, draft, revise and check its own output across several passes, often handing parts of the job to other models.

children.name: Outlining and Plot Structure
children.blurb: Outlining and plot structure covers the planning layer of narrative work, the stage where a story's events are ordered, its turns placed, and its ending decided before or alongside drafting.

children.name: Character Voice and Dialogue
children.blurb: Character voice and dialogue covers the craft of making a fictional person sound like themselves on the page, in a script, or in a game, and it now includes the use of language models to draft, extend, or test that speech.

children.name: World-Building and Continuity
children.blurb: World-building and continuity is the craft of keeping a fictional setting coherent across many pieces of work, whether that is a novel series, a game franchise, a television writers room or a tabletop campaign.

children.name: Developmental Editing
children.blurb: Developmental editing is the work of shaping a manuscript at the level of structure, argument, character and pacing rather than at the level of commas and typos.

sections.body: Literary arts and narrative design covers the use of AI systems to draft, structure, revise and maintain long works of fiction and nonfiction. In practice, writers use language models to generate scene drafts, propose plot alternatives, produce character dialogue in a consistent voice, and flag continuity errors across hundreds of pages. Agentic setups chain several models together, one outlining, one drafting, one critiquing, so a manuscript can move through stages with limited manual copying. The work is text generation and text analysis, not authorship in the legal sense, and the human writer still sets intent, selects output and decides what stays. Tools in this space also track names, dates, places and objects so a long project does not contradict itself.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Short-form drafting is largely solved. Models produce fluent prose, competent dialogue and usable outlines on demand, and continuity checking against a supplied story bible is reliable when the bible is complete. What is not solved is sustained coherence over a full novel, where tone drifts, subplots stall and characters flatten across many chapters. Evaluation is weak because quality in fiction is contested and no benchmark captures it well. Rights and provenance remain unsettled, and the site tracks 92 active intellectual property lawsuits, a reminder that training data and output ownership are still being argued in court. Nothing here is legal advice, and writers with specific concerns should consult a qualified professional.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The five pages follow the arc of a project rather than a list of tools. Outlining and Plot Structure comes first, covering beat sheets, act structure and the generation of branching plot options before prose exists. Agentic Drafting and Multi-Model Workflows then handles the machinery of turning an outline into scenes, including how to route tasks between models and keep a draft moving. Character Voice and Dialogue narrows to the hardest craft problem, making distinct speakers sound like themselves across a long manuscript. World-Building and Continuity covers the reference layer, the story bible and the automated checks that catch contradictions in names, timelines and physical details. Developmental Editing closes the sequence, addressing structural critique, pacing notes and revision passes at the level of the whole work rather than the sentence.
